result.area: output ordering, streams, flushing and exit status

divergences.refOutput: stdout = "usage: test15_executable [-h] --a A --b B --c C --d D\n" (54 bytes), exit 2
divergences.note: REPRO: run with stderr CLOSED, e.g. `/workspace/dataset/test15_executable --a x >/tmp/o 2>&-`. When fd 2 is closed CPython sets sys.stderr = None; argparse's error() does print_usage(_sys.stderr), and print_usage(file=None) defaults to _sys.stdout, so the usage block is emitted on STDOUT. The port's ArgumentParser.error() in /output/lib/cli/argparse.mjs:70 writes formatUsage() unconditionally to process.stderr, so stdout stays empty. Reproduces for every argparse failure path: `--a x`, no args at all, `--a x --b y --c z --d z --e q`. The `prog: error: msg` second line is NOT redirected (it stays swallowed) in either program - only the usage line moves.

divergences.refOutput: exit 120; stderr = "Exception ignored in: <_io.TextIOWrapper name='<stdout>' mode='w' encoding='utf-8'>\nOSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device\n"
divergences.portOutput:
exit 1; stderr = Node crash dump: "node:events:495
      throw er; // Unhandled 'error' event
...Error: ENOSPC: no space left on device, write
    at writeSync (node:fs:929:3)...at ArgumentParser.printHelp (file:///output/lib/cli/argparse.mjs:72:20)...Node.js v18.19.1
"
divergences.note: REPRO: `/workspace/dataset/test15_executable --help >/dev/full`. Reference buffers the 142-byte help text, sys.exit(0) runs, then Py_FinalizeEx's flush_std_files fails -> CPython's "flush failed at shutdown" status 120. The port writes help synchronously, the write throws ENOSPC as an unhandled 'error' event on process.stdout and Node dies with 1. Identical divergence with a read-only stdout fd: `--help 0</etc/hostname 1>&0` gives ref exit 120 / EBADF "Exception ignored in", port exit 1 / Node EBADF dump.

divergences.refOutput:
exit 1; stderr = "Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "test15.py", line 17, in <module>
OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device
[PYI-<pid>:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test15' due to unhandled exception!
"
divergences.note: REPRO: `A=$(head -c 5990 /dev/zero | tr '\0' 'A'); /workspace/dataset/test15_executable --a "$A" --b y --c z --d z >/dev/full`. Once total stdout exceeds the 8192-byte block buffer, print() itself performs the write, so the reference raises OSError from inside the script and exits 1 with a real test15.py traceback. printBytes/console.log in the port swallows the write error and main() returns 0. Threshold measured: 5980 A's -> 8187 stdout bytes -> ref exit 0; 5990 A's -> 8200 bytes -> ref exit 1. The blamed source line tracks which print() overflows the buffer: line 17 (print(dec1)) at 5990 A's, line 15 (print(enc1)) at 6000 A's. Same divergence with a read-only stdout fd (EBADF) instead of /dev/full.

divergences.refOutput: exit 120 (stderr content discarded by the redirect)
divergences.note: REPRO: `/workspace/dataset/test15_executable --a x 2>/dev/full`. Reference: argparse writes usage + error to buffered stderr, sys.exit(2), then the shutdown flush of stderr fails -> status 120 overrides 2. Port: the process.stderr write throws ENOSPC as an unhandled 'error' event -> Node exit 1. Note plain `--a x 2>/dev/null` and `2>&-` both give exit 2 in each program, so only the write-error case diverges.

divergences.refOutput:
exit 0; stderr = "Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 1, in <module>
OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device
Exception ignored in: <_io.TextIOWrapper name='<stdout>' mode='w' encoding='utf-8'>
OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device
" (246 bytes)
divergences.note: REPRO: `/workspace/dataset/test15_executable --a hello --b world --c z --d 2g >/dev/full`. Small output stays in the 8192-byte buffer, so the failure surfaces twice at shutdown: once from the PyInstaller bootloader's `PyRun_SimpleString("import sys; sys.stdout.flush(); ...")` (the `<string>`, line 1 frame) and once from Py_FinalizeEx (the "Exception ignored in" line). Exit stays 0 in both. Same shape with a read-only stdout fd, which yields "OSError: [Errno 9] Bad file descriptor" in both slots.

divergences.refOutput:
exit 0; stderr = "Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 1, in <module>
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'flush'
" (133 bytes)
divergences.note: REPRO: `/workspace/dataset/test15_executable --a hello --b world --c z --d 2g >&-`. With fd 1 closed sys.stdout is None; builtin print() returns silently (hence no stdout error and exit 0), but the bootloader's flush string still dereferences None. The port emits nothing. The same 3-line block is APPENDED after the normal traceback in the decode-failure variant `--a x --b y --c 0 --d z >&-` (ref stderr 6 lines + these 3, exit 1; port only the 6, exit 1), and after the large-output variant.

divergences.refOutput:
exit 0; stderr = the full 142-byte help text: "usage: test15_executable [-h] --a A --b B --c C --d D

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --a A
  --b B
  --c C

divergences.portOutput: exit 0; stderr = "" (0 bytes), stdout = "" (0 bytes) - the help text is lost entirely
divergences.note: REPRO: `/workspace/dataset/test15_executable --help >&- 2>/tmp/e`. Mirror image of the stderr-closed finding: print_help(file=None) resolves to sys.stdout = None, then argparse's _print_message falls back to sys.stderr, so the whole help block lands on STDERR. The port's printHelp writes to a dead process.stdout and drops it.

divergences.refOutput:
exit 0; stderr = "Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 1, in <module>
BrokenPipeError: [Errno 32] Broken pipe
Exception ignored in: <_io.TextIOWrapper name='<stdout>' mode='w' encoding='utf-8'>
BrokenPipeError: [Errno 32] Broken pipe
"
divergences.note: REPRO: `/workspace/dataset/test15_executable --a hello --b world --c z --d z | true`. Broken-pipe variant of the flush divergence; exit status matches (0) but stderr does not. Large-output variant `--a $(6000 A's) ... | true` gives ref "Traceback ... File \"test15.py\", line 15 ... BrokenPipeError" + the PYI footer at exit 0, port silent. `--a $(6000 A's) ... | head -c 100` writes the same 100 stdout bytes in both but ref adds the `<string>` BrokenPipeError block. `--help | true` gives ref "Exception ignored in: ... BrokenPipeError" (exit 0) vs port a full Node EPIPE `Unhandled 'error' event` dump (exit 0).

triedAndClean: Success path byte-exactness: stdout is exactly 4 newline-terminated lines with no trailing extras, verified with wc -l / wc -c / od -c for plain ASCII, empty --a, all four args empty (16 bytes), embedded newline, '1111', emoji/euro, 33-char base58 --c (100 bytes), quotes, backslashes, latin-1 chars - identical byte counts and content in both.

Exit statuses under normal stdio (pipe): success 0, decode failure 1, argparse failure 2 (missing required, unrecognized argument, expected one argument, unknown --zzz, extra positional, no args at all), --help 0, -h 0, --help mid-args 0. All match.

Nothing reaches stdout when either decode fails: 0 bytes of stdout for --c invalid, --d invalid, both invalid, --c invalid with empty --d, empty --c with invalid --d. Confirmed with wc -c on a redirected file, not just eyeballing.

Blame attribution when both --c and --d are invalid: reference blames --c (test15.py line 13 frame) and the port matches exactly; --c valid / --d invalid correctly moves to line 14 in both. Also checked with distinct invalid chars ('0' vs '0', 'l' vs 'I', 'O' vs 'O') so the message text could not mask a swapped frame.
stdout to a regular file: 32-byte small case and 8214-byte large case byte-identical, exit 0 both. Append mode (>>) identical.
stdout to a tty (via `script -q -c`, i.e. line-buffered mode): success case byte-identical; decode-failure case byte-identical including the stdout/stderr interleaving order and PYI footer position.

Merged streams 2>&1 into one file: decode failure produces 299 identical bytes in both (only the PID field differs); large success output produces 8214 identical bytes in both. No ordering divergence.
stderr unwritable on the decode-failure path: `2>/dev/full` and `2>&-` both give exit 1 with empty stdout in each program - the port's traceback write does not blow up there.
Both fd 1 and fd 2 closed: argparse error exit 2 in both, success exit 0 in both, no output either way.
stdout unwritable on the argparse-error path: `--a x >/dev/full` and `--a x >&-` both exit 2 with matching output (usage goes to the still-open stderr).
--help with stderr closed (`2>&-`): both write the same 142-byte help to stdout, exit 0.
Closed stdin (`0<&-`): success case identical, 22 bytes, exit 0.
Buffer-boundary sweep on /dev/full at --a lengths 5960/5970/5975/5980 (stdout totals 8159-8187 bytes): both programs exit 0, so the divergence is confined to totals above the 8192-byte buffer.
Broad randomized fuzz: 150 cases at seed 777 plus the 20-case hand-built ordering/exit-status batch, all matched on stdout, exit, and stderr.
